newsitem.title: DUBAI: GCC says disappointed with Israel's peace policies.
newsitem.headline: GCC says disappointed with Israel's peace policies.

text.p: The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) attacked Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hardline peace policies with Palestinians.

"Netanyahu will realise one day that the only road towards peace in the region is by activating agreements signed between Israel and the Palestinian Authority," Gulf news agencies quoted GCC Secretary-General Jameel Hujilan as saying in Qatar late on Saturday.
"Peace is the only way for Israel...to stabilise its ties with Arab states."

Israel signed a deal with the PLO last year to withdraw troops from major West Bank towns, but delayed a pullout from Hebron after a wave of militant Islamic suicide bombings in Israel in February and March.
Netanyahu, who ousted the government that negotiated the deal in elections last May, put the agreement on hold, saying changes were needed to enhance security for Jewish settlers.
Israelis and Palestinians have failed in two weeks of U.S.-mediated talks to agree on a pullout.
Qatar and Oman are the only states in the six-nation GCC that have allowed Israel to set up trade missions. Oman has also opened a commercial office in Tel Aviv.
But both Gulf States have stopped short of full diplomatic ties pending resolution of all Arab-Israeli conflicts in line with a GCC resolution.
The GCC also includes Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.
